question: The function of a steering system is to convert the rotary movement of the steering wheel into:

options.text: angular turn of the front wheels
angular turns of the rear wheels
angular velocity of the front wheels
linear motion of the front wheels

solution:
The correct answer is __angular turn of the front wheels.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The steering system__ is responsible for converting the rotary motion of the steering wheel into an angular turn of the front wheels.
 
• The steering system ensures precise control of the vehicle's direction.
 
• It primarily affects the front wheels, which are used to navigate the vehicle.
 
• Modern steering systems include power steering to enhance the driver's comfort and reduce effort.
 
• Proper functioning of the steering system is critical for safety and maneuverability.
 
• The system works through a combination of mechanical, hydraulic, or electric components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Rear-Wheel Steering:**

 
 
• In some specific vehicles, rear-wheel steering is used for better control and maneuverability.
 
• This is mostly employed in advanced or specialized vehicles like forklifts or high-performance cars.
 
 
 
• **Power Steering: **
 
 
• Power steering reduces the effort needed by the driver to steer the vehicle.
 
• It uses hydraulic or electric systems to assist in turning the wheels.
 
 
 
• **Types of Steering Mechanisms:**
 
 
• Rack and Pinion Steering: Converts rotary motion to linear motion for better control.
 
• Recirculating Ball Steering: Commonly used in heavier vehicles.
